chapters.title: Chapter 1667: Top Rank!
paragraphs: After putting away the Soul Devouring Sword, Max slowly lifted his gaze and looked toward the remaining participants gathered around the platform.
At that moment, the entire battlefield had already fallen into complete silence.
Nobody spoke.
Nobody moved recklessly.

The scene of Ray’s defeat still lingered vividly within everyone’s minds. From the moment Ray revealed the terrifying power of the Pseudo Cosmic Path until he unleashed the horrifying Soul Devouring Sword, everyone had believed Max would eventually be forced into despair.
Yet in the end—
Ray had still been defeated completely.
Not only had Max survived the Soul Devouring Sword, he had even taken the weapon away directly before eliminating Ray afterward.
That result had shaken everyone deeply.

Especially after witnessing the terrifying physical strength, monstrous regeneration, overwhelming swordsmanship, and incomprehensible soul abilities Max possessed, the remaining participants no longer viewed him as someone within the same level as themselves.
Many of them now looked at Max with genuine fear hidden within their eyes.
Max naturally noticed all of this clearly.
Then, while holding the seven colored lightning sword casually in his hand, he spoke calmly.
"If you do not want to be eliminated," Max said while glancing across the platform slowly, "then you should leave now."
Although his voice was calm, nobody dared ignore those words.
The surrounding participants immediately exchanged uneasy looks with one another.
Nobody stepped forward.
Nobody challenged him.
After all, even Ray Willer, who possessed traces of a Pseudo Cosmic Path and had even used the terrifying Soul Devouring Sword, had still ended up defeated by Max.
If even someone like Ray could not contend against him, then what qualifications did the rest of them possess to fight Max directly?
That thought alone caused many people to lose the courage to remain on the platform.
Very quickly, figures began retreating one after another.
Some left silently.
Others looked toward Max with complicated expressions before turning around and departing from the platform entirely.
Nobody wished to gamble their survival against a monster like him.
Meanwhile, Jonathan remained standing where he was for a few moments longer.
His eyes stayed fixed upon Max while countless thoughts flashed through his mind silently.
Then eventually, a faint smile appeared on Jonathan’s face.
"You truly are terrifying," Jonathan admitted honestly.
There was no hostility in his voice.
Only seriousness.
Then Jonathan slowly turned around before speaking one final sentence.
"I will see you again later, Max."
The moment those words fell, Jonathan’s figure disappeared from the platform.
Julie glanced toward Max once more after Jonathan left.
Her beautiful eyes still carried traces of shock from everything she had witnessed today.
However, she said nothing.
A moment later, Julie also departed alongside Jonathan, leaving the platform completely.
Soon afterward, the once crowded battlefield became almost entirely empty.
"Nice," Max muttered softly while looking toward the cave behind the platform. "Let’s record all the treasures here before moving forward."
After finishing his battle against Ray, Max no longer wasted any time.

He directly entered the cave hidden behind the platform while faint seven colored lightning still flickered around his body. The interior of the cave was filled with numerous treasures radiating powerful fluctuations. Some emitted dense soul aura while others contained astonishing elemental energy.
Max calmly walked toward the center of the cave before placing his name onto the treasure record formation left behind by the Soul Sealing Painting.
The moment his spiritual aura entered the formation, the ownership record for all treasures within the cave instantly changed to his name.
After finishing everything there, Max immediately left the platform and headed toward the remaining areas of the eighth layer.
From that moment onward, almost nobody dared challenge him anymore.
Every participant who saw Max approaching instinctively chose to retreat voluntarily. Some people even abandoned platforms immediately after sensing his aura from afar.
The battle against Ray had already completely established Max’s dominance throughout the tower.
As a result, Max moved through the eighth layer almost unhindered.
Platform after platform.
Cave after cave.
Max continuously recorded every treasure he encountered beneath his name before quickly proceeding deeper into the tower.
Eventually, he arrived at the ninth layer.

The pressure within the ninth layer was far more terrifying than before. The soul suppression filling the surrounding environment had already reached an astonishing level, causing even ordinary peak Law Refinement Realm geniuses to struggle merely standing there.
However, Max remained completely unaffected.
With the support of the Dimension of Soul and his overwhelming physical strength, the terrifying suppression inside the ninth layer no longer posed much threat to him.
Because of that, Max once again began recording treasures rapidly.
However, despite possessing enough strength to monopolize everything within the tower, Max did not take every single platform for himself.
He deliberately left several valuable platforms untouched.
Some were left for Jonathan.
Some were left for Julie.
Others were left for the remaining capable geniuses still climbing the tower.
Max naturally understood that completely monopolizing every opportunity would only create unnecessary hostility from everyone present.
More importantly, he simply did not need everything.
After recording the final treasure at the peak of the ninth layer, Max slowly raised his head and looked toward the vast surroundings beneath him.
Then, after confirming there was nothing else worth staying for, Max finally turned around and left the tower completely.
At the same time, outside the tower, the enormous ranking screen floating above the battlefield suddenly flickered brightly.
The moment Ray Willer had been eliminated earlier, half of his accumulated killing points had automatically transferred directly to Max according to the rules of the Soul Sealing Painting.
Because of that—
Max’s ranking instantly soared to the very top.
Soon, the updated ranking list appeared clearly before everyone.
Max Morgan — 18,940 KP
Jonathan Myres — 13,220 KP
Julie Ravencrest — 12,870 KP
Marcus Vale — 10,430 KP
Serena Ashbourne — 9,980 KP
Darius Holt — 9,110 KP
Ethan Blackwell — 8,760 KP
Alicia Moonfall — 8,340 KP
Leon Draven — 7,950 KP
Victor Kane — 7,510 Kp
The moment the ranking list updated, countless participants inside and outside the Soul Sealing Painting immediately erupted into uproar.
Because Max Morgan’s name now stood firmly at the very top.

chapters.title: Chapter 1668: End of the Third Trial!
paragraphs: Soon, Max arrived at a vast open area where several other participants had already gathered.
The moment he appeared, many people instinctively turned toward him.
However, compared to the beginning of the trial, the atmosphere now felt completely different.

Earlier, when the Soul Sealing Painting first opened, hundreds of geniuses had entered this world together. Everywhere one looked, powerful participants could be seen fighting for treasures, hunting monsters, and competing against one another.
But now—
The number of remaining participants had dropped drastically.
The once crowded trial world had become strangely quiet.
Max calmly swept his gaze across the surroundings while his Dimensional Sovereign Body spread outward silently.
In the next instant, he accurately perceived the number of people still remaining alive inside the Soul Sealing Painting.
"There are only around twenty participants left here," Max muttered softly.
A thoughtful expression appeared across his face afterward.
"I suppose this trial is about to end."

Max still clearly remembered the rules Elder Cael had announced before the trial began. The Soul Sealing Painting would officially close once the total number of remaining participants dropped below fifty.
At the moment, there were only around twenty people gathered here.
As for the others, Max knew several participants were still inside the Tower of Treasure searching for opportunities.
However, even after counting those individuals, the total number remaining inside the Soul Sealing Painting should no longer exceed fifty by much.
Because of that, Max understood very clearly that it was probably only a matter of minutes before the trial officially concluded.
Then suddenly, another thought surfaced within his mind.
"That reminds me..." Max muttered while narrowing his eyes slightly in thought.
"There is only one internal trial ground called the Tower of Treasure inside this Soul Sealing Painting."
The more Max thought about it, the more certain he became.
If even this preparatory trial possessed a special inheritance zone like the Tower of Treasure, then the real Cosmic Ascension Conference would undoubtedly be far more grand and terrifying.
After all, the Cosmic Ascension Conference was held within the Eternal Hourglass itself.
That place gathered geniuses from countless worlds, star domains, and major forces.
The number of participants entering the Cosmic Ascension Conference would likely reach an absolutely terrifying level.
Possibly even trillions.
Because of that, it would naturally be impossible for everyone to compete inside only one area.
Which meant—
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, there should be hundreds or perhaps even thousands of similar internal trial grounds scattered throughout the conference world.
The moment he realized this, excitement gradually appeared within Max’s eyes.

If every one of those internal trials contained treasures and opportunities comparable to the Tower of Treasure, then the Cosmic Ascension Conference would truly become a heaven-defying land of fortune.

"With the treasures I gathered from the Tower of Treasure..." Max muttered softly while a faint smile slowly appeared across his face, "I should be able to break through to the tenth level of the Law Awakening Realm."
At the same time, another thought surfaced in his mind.
"And after that, I should finally be able to open the fourth Divine Vein of the Seven Divine Veins..."
"The Vein of Speed."
Just thinking about it caused anticipation to rise within Max’s heart.
The Vein of Strength had already granted him terrifying physical might.
The Vein of Origin had strengthened his foundations tremendously.
The Vein of Vitality had given him astonishing regenerative power.
Because of that, Max naturally understood how terrifying the Vein of Speed would likely become once it awakened completely.
And that was not his only gain from this trial.
Max’s smile deepened slightly.
"I also obtained an extremely powerful sword art that I still have not fully mastered yet," he murmured thoughtfully.
The Saint Origin Sword Art still possessed enormous untapped potential.
Especially after combining it with traces of the half-formed Emotion Severing Cosmic Path, Max could already vaguely sense how terrifying that sword art might eventually become in the future.
On top of that, this battle had also allowed him to personally witness the power of a Pseudo Cosmic Path.
That experience alone was incredibly valuable.
After all, directly experiencing such power firsthand was far more beneficial than merely hearing stories about it from others.
Eventually, Max let out a faint chuckle.
"I suppose this trip to the Violet Star Palace was truly worth it."
Just as Max was quietly thinking about everything he had gained from this trial, a familiar mechanical voice suddenly echoed throughout the entire Soul Sealing Painting.
At the same time, countless glowing notifications appeared before every remaining participant.
[Total remaining participants have been reduced to fifty.]
[Conditions for completion of the third trial have been fulfilled.]
[The third trial of the Soul Sealing Painting has officially concluded.]
The moment those notifications appeared, the expressions of the surrounding participants changed immediately.
Then, before anyone could react further, the surrounding world suddenly began trembling faintly.
A mysterious spatial force descended upon the entire Soul Sealing Painting.
Max instantly felt the connection between his soul and this world gradually weakening.
At the same time, nearby participants began disappearing one after another.
Some vanished while still standing silently in place.
Others revealed relieved expressions before their bodies gradually dissolved into particles of light.
The entire area became increasingly empty within only a few moments.
The remaining geniuses also vanished rapidly under the power of the Soul Sealing Painting.
Clearly, everyone was now being forcefully returned to their original bodies outside.
Max calmly observed everything around him while faint spatial ripples gradually surrounded his own body as well.
The surrounding scenery began turning blurry little by little.
Even the enormous sky above the Soul Sealing Painting gradually distorted as though the entire world itself was fading away.
Then another notification appeared before Max’s eyes.
[Calculating final rankings...]
[Calculating rewards...]
[Preparing participant transfer...]
A faint smile appeared across Max’s face after seeing those notifications.
This trial had brought him enormous gains.

Not only had he obtained treasures capable of helping him reach the tenth level of the Law Awakening Realm, he had also unlocked the Dimension of Soul, obtained the Soul Devouring Sword, witnessed a Pseudo Cosmic Path firsthand, and further strengthened his understanding of the Saint Origin Sword Art.
Compared to those rewards, even his first-place ranking felt secondary.
Soon afterward, the spatial force surrounding Max intensified completely.
Countless particles of light emerged around his body as his figure gradually began fading away from the Soul Sealing Painting.
Then—
Max disappeared completely.

The Vein of Origin had strengthened his foundations tremendously.
The Vein of Vitality had given him astonishing regenerative power.
Because of that, Max naturally understood how terrifying the Vein of Speed would likely become once it awakened completely.
And that was not his only gain from this trial.
Max’s smile deepened slightly.
"I also obtained an extremely powerful sword art that I still have not fully mastered yet," he murmured thoughtfully.
The Saint Origin Sword Art still possessed enormous untapped potential.
Especially after combining it with traces of the half-formed Emotion Severing Cosmic Path, Max could already vaguely sense how terrifying that sword art might eventually become in the future.
On top of that, this battle had also allowed him to personally witness the power of a Pseudo Cosmic Path.
That experience alone was incredibly valuable.
After all, directly experiencing such power firsthand was far more beneficial than merely hearing stories about it from others.
Eventually, Max let out a faint chuckle.
"I suppose this trip to the Violet Star Palace was truly worth it."
Just as Max was quietly thinking about everything he had gained from this trial, a familiar mechanical voice suddenly echoed throughout the entire Soul Sealing Painting.
At the same time, countless glowing notifications appeared before every remaining participant.
[Total remaining participants have been reduced to fifty.]
[Conditions for completion of the third trial have been fulfilled.]
[The third trial of the Soul Sealing Painting has officially concluded.]
The moment those notifications appeared, the expressions of the surrounding participants changed immediately.
Then, before anyone could react further, the surrounding world suddenly began trembling faintly.
A mysterious spatial force descended upon the entire Soul Sealing Painting.
Max instantly felt the connection between his soul and this world gradually weakening.
At the same time, nearby participants began disappearing one after another.
Some vanished while still standing silently in place.
Others revealed relieved expressions before their bodies gradually dissolved into particles of light.
The entire area became increasingly empty within only a few moments.
The remaining geniuses also vanished rapidly under the power of the Soul Sealing Painting.
Clearly, everyone was now being forcefully returned to their original bodies outside.
Max calmly observed everything around him while faint spatial ripples gradually surrounded his own body as well.
The surrounding scenery began turning blurry little by little.
Even the enormous sky above the Soul Sealing Painting gradually distorted as though the entire world itself was fading away.
Then another notification appeared before Max’s eyes.
[Calculating final rankings...]
[Calculating rewards...]
[Preparing participant transfer...]
A faint smile appeared across Max’s face after seeing those notifications.
This trial had brought him enormous gains.

Not only had he obtained treasures capable of helping him reach the tenth level of the Law Awakening Realm, he had also unlocked the Dimension of Soul, obtained the Soul Devouring Sword, witnessed a Pseudo Cosmic Path firsthand, and further strengthened his understanding of the Saint Origin Sword Art.
Compared to those rewards, even his first-place ranking felt secondary.
Soon afterward, the spatial force surrounding Max intensified completely.
Countless particles of light emerged around his body as his figure gradually began fading away from the Soul Sealing Painting.
Then—
Max disappeared completely.

chapters.title: Chapter 1669: End of Smelting Trial!
paragraphs: Appearing outside the Soul Sealing Painting once again, Max immediately felt a brief sense of discomfort spread throughout his body.
It felt as though his soul and physical body had momentarily fallen out of synchronization after remaining separated for such a long period of time inside the Soul Sealing Painting world.
However, that strange sensation disappeared almost instantly.
Max quickly regained full control over his body as his consciousness stabilized completely.
At the same time, countless other participants also began opening their eyes one after another throughout the massive square of the Violet Star Palace.
Some people revealed exhausted expressions.
Others still appeared shaken from the brutal battles inside the Soul Sealing Painting.
A few participants even looked relieved merely to have survived until the end.
Meanwhile, high above the square, the enormous Soul Sealing Painting floating in the sky gradually dimmed before slowly returning to its previous calm state.
Then Elder Cael stepped forward once again.
The old man swept his gaze across the countless gathered disciples and elders before speaking with a calm yet authoritative voice that echoed throughout the entire square.
"The third trial has officially concluded."
The moment those words fell, the entire crowd immediately became noisy once again.

After all, the third trial had undoubtedly been the most brutal and intense trial so far. Countless geniuses had been eliminated throughout the process, while the battles that occurred inside the Tower of Treasure had shaken nearly everyone watching from outside.
Especially the confrontation between Max and Ray Willer.
That battle alone had already become the center of discussion among countless disciples and elders present.
At that moment, Elder Cael slowly raised his hand.
The noisy crowd gradually quieted down afterward.
Then Elder Cael continued speaking.
"Next..." he said calmly, "look toward the ranking screen."
The moment his voice fell, the enormous screen floating above the square suddenly flickered brightly.
Soon afterward, a massive ranking list appeared before everyone’s eyes.
The moment the rankings became visible, countless gazes instantly focused upon the very top.
Then—
The expressions of numerous elders changed immediately.
Max Morgan — 18,940 Points
Jonathan Myres — 13,220 Points
Julie Ravencrest — 12,870 Points
Marcus Vale — 10,430 Points
Serena Ashbourne — 9,980 Points
Darius Holt — 9,110 Points
Ethan Blackwell — 8,760 Points
Alicia Moonfall — 8,340 Points
Leon Draven — 7,950 Points
Victor Kane — 7,510 Points
Silence spread briefly across the square.
Then the entire place erupted into uproar.
"What?!"
"Max Morgan again?!"
"He actually took first place in the third trial too?!"
Many disciples revealed expressions filled with disbelief while numerous elders stared at the rankings with shocked expressions.
This was already the third trial.
And yet—
Max had once again stood at the very top.
Earlier, many people had still believed his first-place performance in the previous two trials might have been due to luck, hidden opportunities, or favorable circumstances.
But now, after the third trial ended with Max taking first place yet again, those doubts gradually began disappearing.
Because this result could no longer be explained away so easily.
The third trial was the harshest and most dangerous trial among all three.
It tested survival ability, combat strength, adaptability, comprehension, and even one’s courage in fighting against other geniuses.
Yet despite all of that—
Max still dominated the rankings completely.
Many elders exchanged serious glances with one another afterward.
Even some hidden experts observing from afar revealed thoughtful expressions.
Meanwhile, within the crowd, the expressions of the Violet Star Palace disciples became increasingly complicated.
Because everyone now understood one terrifying truth.
A true monster had appeared in this Smelting Trial.
After the uproar caused by the ranking list gradually settled down, Elder Cael once again stepped forward slowly.

The old man stood high above the square while his calm gaze swept across the countless gathered geniuses from the various third-rate forces. For a brief moment, his eyes lingered upon several outstanding participants, especially Max, Jonathan, and Julie, before he finally began speaking once more.
"Now that the results of the third trial have been announced," Elder Cael said calmly, his voice echoing clearly throughout the entire square, "the Smelting Trial has officially come to an end."
The moment those words fell, many disciples revealed complicated expressions.
Some looked excited after gaining tremendous opportunities during the trials.
Others appeared disappointed because they failed to obtain satisfactory results.
However, regardless of their emotions, everyone understood one thing clearly.
This Smelting Trial had been extraordinarily important for all of them.
Not only had it provided them with valuable treasures and opportunities, it had also allowed them to personally witness the terrifying strength possessed by the geniuses of other forces.
Especially after seeing monsters like Max and Ray Willer, many participants finally realized just how vast the outside world truly was.
Meanwhile, Elder Cael continued speaking.
"The true purpose of this Smelting Trial was never merely competition," he said slowly. "It was created to prepare all of you for the coming Cosmic Ascension Conference."
The moment the words "Cosmic Ascension Conference" were mentioned, the expressions of countless geniuses immediately became serious.
Even the surrounding elders revealed solemn looks.
After all, compared to the Smelting Trial, the Cosmic Ascension Conference was the true grand stage of the younger generation.
That was where geniuses from countless worlds and powerful forces would gather together.
Compared to those monstrous talents, the participants present here were still only geniuses among third-rate forces.
"There are only three months remaining before the Cosmic Ascension Conference officially begins," Elder Cael continued calmly. "I hope all of you will use this remaining time wisely."
His gaze gradually sharpened slightly afterward.

"The Cosmic Ascension Conference is filled with countless dangers, opportunities, and monstrous geniuses beyond your imagination. Whether you rise or fall there will ultimately depend upon your own abilities."
Then, for the first time since the trials began, a faint smile appeared on Elder Cael’s aged face.
"Still," he said slowly, "I sincerely wish all of you the very best."
"I hope that among the geniuses gathered here today, some of you will one day shine brilliantly throughout the Divine Realm itself."
The surrounding disciples immediately became excited after hearing those words.
Even some elders nodded lightly in agreement.
Soon afterward, Elder Cael lightly waved his hand before speaking once more.
"Finally..." he said, "before everyone departs from the Violet Star Palace, a small banquet will be held tomorrow evening."
The atmosphere within the square instantly relaxed slightly afterward.
"A banquet?" many disciples muttered excitedly.
Elder Cael smiled faintly.
"You have all worked hard throughout these trials," he continued. "Take this opportunity to relax, exchange experiences, and enjoy yourselves before this gathering officially comes to an end."
The surrounding disciples immediately became much more lively after hearing that announcement.
Some people began discussing the banquet excitedly with their companions.
Others discussed the results of the Smelting Trial once again.
Meanwhile, many gazes still continued drifting toward Max from time to time.
After all, regardless of the banquet or the end of the trials, everyone understood one thing clearly.
The greatest topic of this entire Smelting Trial—
Was undoubtedly Max Morgan.

chapters.title: Chapter 1670: Jonathan’s Plea for Help!
paragraphs: With Elder Cael’s final announcement, the tense atmosphere lingering throughout the square gradually began fading away.
The Smelting Trial had finally ended.

Soon afterward, the countless gathered disciples and elders slowly began dispersing in different directions. Various third-rate forces regrouped together while discussions about the trials echoed endlessly throughout the Violet Star Palace.
Some disciples excitedly discussed the treasures they obtained.
Others spoke about the brutal battles inside the Soul Sealing Painting.
However, the topic mentioned most frequently by nearly everyone remained the same.
Max Morgan.
Many elders looked toward him with complicated expressions while younger geniuses either admired him, feared him, or envied him deeply.
Meanwhile, Max calmly walked through the dispersing crowd before eventually arriving beside Isabella and Lucia.
The moment Isabella saw him approaching safely, the tension within her expression visibly relaxed.
"You are finally back," Isabella said softly while looking at him carefully. "Do you know how terrifying your battle with Ray looked from outside?"
Even now, traces of lingering shock could still be seen within her beautiful eyes.

Lucia immediately nodded in agreement afterward. Even though they weren’t present at the platform where the battle between Ray and Max took place, they weren’t far from it. They could see and heard the battle from the nearby platforms at the 8th layer.
"That Soul Devouring Sword was horrifying," Lucia admitted honestly. "For a moment, even I thought something might happen to you."
Max simply smiled faintly after hearing their words.
"Unfortunately for Ray," Max replied calmly, "things did not go according to his plans."
Lucia immediately rolled her eyes slightly.
"You say that so casually," she muttered. "But you nearly scared everyone half to death."
Even Isabella revealed a helpless smile afterward.
Clearly, despite Max acting calm now, the battle earlier had genuinely shocked many people.
Then suddenly—
"Max."
A calm voice sounded from nearby.
The three of them immediately turned toward the source of the voice.
Jonathan slowly walked toward them.
His expression remained calm as usual, but his eyes carried obvious seriousness while looking at Max.
The surrounding disciples instinctively became quieter after noticing Jonathan approaching.
After all, Jonathan was still one of the most famous geniuses present within the Smelting Trial.
And after the third trial rankings, everyone clearly understood that Jonathan and Max were now considered two of the strongest younger generation geniuses among the gathered third-rate forces.
Jonathan eventually stopped several steps away from Max.
Then he spoke directly.
"I would like to speak with you privately for a moment," Jonathan said calmly.
Lucia immediately narrowed her eyes slightly while Isabella became somewhat thoughtful.
However, Max himself did not appear surprised.
"What is it about?" Max asked calmly.
Jonathan remained silent briefly before replying.
"It concerns the Cosmic Ascension Conference."
Hearing those words immediately caused Max’s interest to rise slightly.
Jonathan then continued.
"Julie is also involved in this discussion."
At the mention of Julie’s name, Max became even more thoughtful.
Clearly, this was not some casual conversation.
After a few moments of silence, Max finally nodded lightly.
"Alright," Max agreed calmly. "Where do you want to meet?"
A faint smile appeared on Jonathan’s face afterward.
"There is a quiet pavilion near the eastern side of the Violet Star Palace," Jonathan replied. "Julie is already waiting there."
Then Jonathan looked directly into Max’s eyes.
"There are some things we believe you should know before the Cosmic Ascension Conference begins."
Max stared at Jonathan briefly before eventually smiling faintly.
"Interesting," he muttered softly.
Then he nodded once more.
"Lead the way."
Following Jonathan through the quiet pathways of the Violet Star Palace, Max soon arrived at a secluded area far away from the noisy gathering square.
The surroundings here were much calmer.

Beautiful spirit trees swayed gently beneath the evening breeze while faint spiritual mist drifted across the pathways. Small streams of clear water flowed peacefully nearby, creating a tranquil atmosphere completely different from the tense environment of the Smelting Trial earlier.
At the center of the area stood an elegant pavilion built beside a calm spirit lake.
Julie was already waiting there.

She sat quietly near the edge of the pavilion while staring toward the surface of the lake thoughtfully. The faint moonlight reflecting across the water illuminated her expression softly, yet despite the peaceful surroundings, the atmosphere around her felt strangely heavy.
The moment Max and Jonathan stepped into the pavilion, Julie slowly raised her gaze toward them.
However—
The instant Max entered the pavilion, his eyes narrowed slightly.
Because he immediately sensed something wrong.
The atmosphere here was far too tense.
Neither Jonathan nor Julie appeared relaxed in the slightest. Their expressions carried obvious seriousness, and even the spiritual energy fluctuations around them felt faintly unstable.
This was not the atmosphere of people casually discussing the Cosmic Ascension Conference.
Max’s Dimensional Sovereign Body silently spread outward for a brief moment before retracting once again.
Then his expression became calm.
At that moment, Max already understood something clearly.
Jonathan had not called him here merely to discuss matters related to the Cosmic Ascension Conference.
There was something else.
And whatever it was, it seemed important enough for both Jonathan and Julie to personally wait for him here.
Because of that, Max no longer wasted time.
He directly walked into the pavilion before stopping in front of the two of them calmly.
Then he spoke immediately.
"You did not call me here to talk about the Cosmic Ascension Conference."
The moment those words fell, Jonathan and Julie’s expressions changed slightly.
Max’s eyes calmly swept across both of them before he continued speaking.
"So stop wasting time."
His voice remained completely calm.
"What is it that you actually want?"

Jonathan remained silent for several moments after hearing Max’s question. Clearly, whatever he wanted to say next was not easy for him to bring up. Even Julie’s expression became visibly heavier as she quietly lowered her gaze for a brief moment.
Eventually, Jonathan took a deep breath before finally speaking.
"We need your help."

The seriousness in his voice immediately caused Max to frown slightly. After everything that happened during the Smelting Trial, Max knew very clearly that people like Jonathan would not casually seek help from others unless the situation was genuinely important.
"What kind of help?" Max asked calmly.

chapters.title: Chapter 1671: Ten Thousand Poison Body!
paragraphs: Jonathan exchanged a glance with Julie first before speaking again.
"Have you ever heard of a physique called the Ten Thousand Poison Body?"
The moment those words entered his ears, Max’s expression changed slightly. Naturally, he had heard of it before.

Back when he was still within the Black Dragon Clan, Max had spent enormous amounts of time reading through ancient records and books related to physiques, bloodlines, cultivation constitutions, and forbidden powers.
Because of that, he possessed at least some understanding regarding the Ten Thousand Poison Body.

"I have heard of it. It is considered one of the most terrifying cursed physiques recorded in the ancient eras. If I remember correctly, the Ten Thousand Poison Body is not a physique people are born with naturally through ordinary bloodline inheritance. Instead, it is something far stranger and far more dangerous."
Max continued.

"It is said that individuals possessing the Ten Thousand Poison Body are cursed by fate itself. The exact origins of the physique remain unclear because even the oldest surviving records regarding it are incomplete. However, one thing has always remained consistent throughout every historical account. The Ten Thousand Poison Body is extremely deadly."
As Max spoke those words, even the atmosphere inside the pavilion gradually became heavier.

"The body of someone possessing this physique naturally generates terrifying poison energy from birth. That poison is not ordinary toxin. It is a highly evolved poisonous force capable of corroding flesh, spiritual energy, bloodlines, organs, and eventually even the soul itself. The truly horrifying aspect of the Ten Thousand Poison Body is that the poison does not merely affect outsiders. It affects the owner as well."
Jonathan’s expression darkened noticeably while Julie’s fingers unconsciously tightened slightly.

"From the moment someone with the Ten Thousand Poison Body is born, their body continuously produces stronger and stronger poison energy over time. At first, the symptoms may remain manageable. However, as the years pass, the poison gradually begins consuming the user from within. Their internal organs weaken first, then their blood, then their meridians, and eventually even their spiritual energy itself becomes poisonous."
Max’s expression gradually became more solemn as he continued.

"In the later stages, even remaining close to someone possessing a fully awakened Ten Thousand Poison Body can become dangerous because their mere presence can spread poison unconsciously into the surrounding environment. Plants wither around them. Spirit beasts die near them. Even powerful cultivators can gradually become infected after prolonged exposure."
The silence inside the pavilion grew increasingly heavy.

"The cruelest part is that the stronger the owner becomes, the stronger the poison becomes as well. That is why the Ten Thousand Poison Body is considered a cursed physique instead of a heaven-defying physique despite its terrifying potential. Although the physique grants overwhelming poisonous power capable of making even powerful cultivators fear them, the owner themselves is also slowly dying the entire time."
Max slowly narrowed his eyes afterward.

"In most historical records, people possessing the Ten Thousand Poison Body rarely live long lives. Many die young. Others lose their sanity from the constant pain and poison corrosion. In some cases, the poison eventually completely loses control and devours both the owner and everyone around them."
The moment Max finished speaking, his gaze slowly shifted toward Julie.
The tension on her face already told him more than enough.

Her expression was unusually strained while a faint sense of exhaustion could be seen hidden deep within her eyes. Even the spiritual aura around her felt slightly unstable now that Max paid closer attention to it.
At that moment, Max immediately understood the situation.
"Is she...?" Max asked quietly while looking toward Jonathan.
Jonathan slowly nodded.
"Yes," he replied heavily. "Julie possesses the Ten Thousand Poison Body."
The atmosphere inside the pavilion instantly became even heavier.

"Right now, we are only able to suppress the poison temporarily using several special treasures," Jonathan continued. "Those treasures prevent the poison from leaking out of her body and affecting the surroundings, but this is only a temporary solution."
Jonathan’s fists tightened slightly afterward.
"The poison inside her body is still growing stronger with time. It is already slowly destroying her from within. Unless we completely remove the poison one day, she will eventually die."
Julie remained silent throughout the entire conversation, but the slight lowering of her gaze already revealed enough.
Jonathan let out a slow breath before continuing again.
"There is only one treasure known to possess the ability to completely erase the poison inside someone with the Ten Thousand Poison Body."
"The Poison Erosion Fruit."
The moment those words were spoken, Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Jonathan’s expression became increasingly solemn afterward.
"However, the Poison Erosion Fruit is unbelievably rare. Some ancient records even claim it has already gone extinct entirely. Finding one is nearly impossible."
Then Jonathan looked directly at Max.
"But according to my sources, the Poison Erosion Fruit still exists."
A faint hope appeared within his eyes afterward.
"And the only force currently known to possibly possess it..."
Jonathan paused briefly before finishing his sentence.
"Is the War God Palace."
Then he continued quietly.
"I heard that you have some connection with the War God Palace."
"That is why we need your help."

The faint instability within her aura.
The unusual tension she constantly carried.
Even the subtle traces of suppression treasures hidden around her body.
Everything finally connected together.

Then he spoke calmly.
"I can help her."
The moment those words fell, both Jonathan and Julie’s expressions changed immediately.
However, before either of them could speak, Max continued.
"But I have two conditions."
His voice remained calm, yet serious.
"And both of those conditions must be agreed to first."
Jonathan immediately stepped forward slightly without even hesitating.
"What are the conditions?" he asked hurriedly.
At that moment, Jonathan no longer cared about anything else.
As long as there was even a possibility of curing Julie’s Ten Thousand Poison Body, he was willing to accept almost any price.

chapters.title: Chapter 1672: Two Conditions!
paragraphs: Max looked directly at Jonathan before speaking calmly.
"My first condition is simple," he said. "I want a chance to kill Ray Willer."
The atmosphere inside the pavilion instantly became heavier.
"I do not care how you arrange it," Max continued while his eyes gradually turned colder. "But I want an opportunity to deal with him personally."
Jonathan’s expression immediately became solemn after hearing those words.
Naturally, he understood why Max wanted Ray dead.
After everything that happened during the Smelting Trial, especially Ray’s attempt to truly kill Max using the Soul Devouring Sword, hatred between the two sides had already become irreconcilable.
However, Jonathan still did not immediately respond.
Because Ray Willer was not an ordinary genius.
He possessed deep ties with the Sword God Palace, and his status there was extremely high.
Helping Max kill someone like Ray would undoubtedly bring enormous trouble afterward.
Still—
Jonathan did not reject the condition.
Seeing Jonathan remain silent instead of objecting outright, Max calmly continued.
"My second condition," Max said slowly, "is that both of you must join a secret force I am currently building."
Jonathan frowned deeply this time.
"A secret force?" he repeated while narrowing his eyes slightly. "What kind of force?"
Max remained silent briefly before leaning slightly closer toward Jonathan.
Then he whispered something quietly into his ear.
"An organization created to kill elves."
The moment those words entered Jonathan’s ears, his expression changed drastically.
"What?!" Jonathan blurted out in shock while staring at Max in disbelief.
Clearly, he had never expected something like this.
The Elf Race was one of the most ancient and powerful races within the Divine Realm. Their foundations were terrifyingly deep, and countless major powers avoided provoking them unnecessarily.
Yet Max was openly speaking about creating a force specifically aimed against them.
Even Julie’s calm expression changed slightly after hearing this.
However, Max himself remained completely calm.
"There is no need for you to panic so much," Max said quietly. "I am not foolish enough to challenge the Elf Race recklessly."
His expression gradually became more serious afterward.
"I would never make a move against them until I am absolutely certain we possess enough strength to confront them directly."
Max’s gaze slowly sharpened.
"And I certainly would not drag my own people toward meaningless deaths."
Jonathan remained silent after hearing those words.
At that moment, he could clearly sense something unusual hidden behind Max’s hatred toward the Elf Race.
This was not simple hostility.
It felt personal.
Very personal.
Then Max looked directly into Jonathan’s eyes once again.
"If you agree to these two conditions," Max said calmly, "then I can help Julie."
Jonathan’s expression tightened slightly.
However, before he could speak, Max continued.
"And what I have in mind is not merely removing the poison inside her body."
The moment those words fell, both Jonathan and Julie’s eyes immediately changed.
A faint smile slowly appeared across Max’s face afterward.
"What I can offer her..." he said quietly, "is something even better."
Silence immediately filled the pavilion.
Then Max finally finished speaking.
"So think carefully before making your choice, Jonathan."
Jonathan fell silent after hearing Max’s conditions.
The pavilion became heavy with tension as he lowered his gaze and began thinking deeply.
Neither condition was simple.

The first meant helping Max create an opportunity to kill Ray Willer, someone closely connected to the Sword God Palace. The second meant joining a secret force aimed at the Elf Race, a terrifying race whose power and foundation were far beyond ordinary forces.
No matter which condition he chose to consider, both carried enormous danger.
For a long while, Jonathan said nothing.
Then his gaze slowly shifted toward Julie.
Julie remained quiet, but the faint weakness hidden in her expression and the exhaustion buried deep within her eyes made Jonathan’s heart tighten.
In the end, nothing mattered more than saving her.
Jonathan slowly clenched his fists.
Then he turned back toward Max.
His jaw tightened, and his voice came out through gritted teeth.
"Fine."
He stared directly into Max’s eyes.
"I accept both conditions."
"You made the correct choice," Max said with a faint smile appearing across his face.
Then, under Jonathan and Julie’s surprised gazes, Max slowly raised his hand and took out a strange fruit.

The fruit radiated chaotic energy fluctuations while crimson and golden flame patterns flickered faintly across its surface. The moment it appeared, the surrounding spiritual energy inside the pavilion immediately became restless.
Jonathan’s eyes narrowed slightly after sensing the extraordinary aura emitted by the fruit.
Meanwhile, Max calmly handed it toward him.

"This is an extremely rare treasure known as a Chaos Fruit," Max explained slowly. "It possesses very miraculous properties. Normally, after consuming it, a person has a high chance of awakening a flame-element Divine Body."
Jonathan’s expression immediately changed after hearing those words.
Even Julie looked shocked now.
Divine Bodies were incredibly rare existences. Countless geniuses throughout the Divine Realm would never obtain such an opportunity even after searching their entire lives.
Yet Max was casually taking out a treasure capable of creating one.
However, Max continued speaking calmly.
"But Julie’s situation is different."
His gaze shifted toward Julie afterward.
"Because she already possesses the Ten Thousand Poison Body, there is a very high possibility that the effects of the Chaos Fruit will mutate after entering her body."
A thoughtful expression appeared across Max’s face as he continued explaining.
"There are two possible outcomes."
"The first possibility is that the Ten Thousand Poison Body itself undergoes an evolution and transforms into an even stronger physique."

"The second possibility is that the Chaos Fruit awakens a completely new Divine Body within her, but because of the poison already fused deeply into her body, the newly awakened physique will likely become a flame-poison type Divine Body instead of an ordinary flame Divine Body."
The pavilion gradually fell silent after hearing his explanation.
Jonathan’s breathing had already become slightly heavier.
Meanwhile, Max calmly continued.
"Regardless of which outcome occurs, the result will still benefit her greatly."
A faint smile slowly appeared on his face afterward.
"Because once the poison becomes fully integrated into her physique instead of remaining a destructive force inside her body, she will no longer need to fear it destroying her from within."
Max looked directly toward Julie.
"In fact," he said calmly, "the poison that once threatened to kill her may eventually become her greatest source of strength instead."

chapters.title: Chapter 1673: Their Choice!
paragraphs: Jonathan slowly reached forward and accepted the Chaos Fruit from Max’s hand.

The moment the fruit entered his grasp, he immediately felt an astonishing wave of energy flowing from within it. Chaotic flame energy continuously circulated across the surface of the fruit while faint crimson-golden patterns flickered like living flames.
Even so—
A trace of hesitation still appeared within Jonathan’s eyes.
He lowered his gaze toward the Chaos Fruit while countless thoughts surfaced within his mind.
What Max had just described sounded far too unbelievable.
A treasure capable of granting someone a Divine Body?
Such a thing should not even exist.

Within the Divine Realm, Divine Bodies were regarded as heaven-defying physiques possessed only by monstrous geniuses blessed by fate itself. Some inherited them through bloodlines while others awakened them through miraculous opportunities beyond imagination.
But a fruit capable of directly granting a Divine Body?
Jonathan had never once heard of such a thing before.
And with his status and background, his knowledge far surpassed that of ordinary geniuses.
If treasures like this truly existed openly within the Divine Realm, there was no way he would not have heard at least rumors regarding them before.
Yet—
He could not recall a single thing related to fruits capable of creating Divine Bodies.
That alone caused deep uncertainty to rise within his heart.
Jonathan’s expression gradually became more conflicted afterward.
Because Julie’s condition was already extremely dangerous.
The Ten Thousand Poison Body was not something that could be treated carelessly. One wrong decision could completely destabilize the poison inside her body and worsen her condition even further.
And that was exactly what Jonathan feared most.
He did not want to gamble recklessly with Julie’s life using something he did not fully understand.
Even if Max had sounded confident earlier, Jonathan still found it difficult to completely trust such an unbelievable treasure immediately.
Meanwhile, Julie quietly observed Jonathan from the side.
She could naturally understand what he was worried about.
After all, even she herself found Max’s explanation difficult to believe completely.
The pavilion gradually became silent once again as Jonathan continued staring at the Chaos Fruit within his hand, clearly hesitating over whether he should truly let Julie consume it or not.
Max quietly observed the hesitation and uncertainty on Jonathan and Julie’s faces and immediately understood what they were worried about.
After all, everything he had just told them sounded far too unbelievable.

A fruit capable of awakening a Divine Body was something that would shake the entire Divine Realm if news of it spread. It was only natural for them to hesitate before trusting something they had never even heard about before.
However, Max did not attempt to persuade them further.
Instead, he simply spoke calmly.
"I already gave you a path," Max said while looking at the two of them. "Now the choice is yours whether you want to walk that path or not."
Neither Jonathan nor Julie responded immediately.
The atmosphere inside the pavilion remained heavy as Jonathan continued holding the Chaos Fruit silently in his hand.
Seeing this, Max slowly turned around.
Then, before leaving, he spoke once more.
"The banquet will be held tomorrow," Max said calmly. "I can wait until then."
His voice remained steady and unhurried.
"I hope that by the time we meet again, the two of you will have already made your decision."
With those final words, Max no longer stayed inside the pavilion.
He calmly walked away while the faint moonlight reflected softly across the spirit lake behind him.
Meanwhile, Jonathan and Julie remained standing silently within the pavilion, both lost deeply within their own thoughts while staring at the Chaos Fruit in Jonathan’s hand.
As for Max, he soon left the quiet area entirely and headed back toward the mansion assigned to the Black Dragon Clan.
On the way back toward the Black Dragon Clan’s mansion, Max continued thinking about Jonathan and Julie’s situation.
The more he thought about it, the more tragic their circumstances seemed.
One carried a cursed physique that slowly poisoned her from the inside while the other desperately searched everywhere for even the slightest chance to save her.
In truth, neither of them had many options left anymore.
Max quietly let out a faint sigh.
"I just hope they make the right choice," he muttered softly.
As an outsider, there was only so much he could do for them. In the end, whether they trusted him or not would ultimately depend entirely upon their own decision.
Soon afterward, Max finally arrived back at the mansion assigned to the Black Dragon Clan.
However, the moment he entered the courtyard, two familiar figures immediately appeared before him.
Lucia crossed her arms while narrowing her eyes suspiciously at him.
"Where exactly did you go?" she asked directly.
Beside her, Isabella also looked toward Max curiously.
Seeing their expressions, Max merely smiled faintly.
"That," he replied casually, "is a secret."
Then he looked at Lucia helplessly before adding, "Besides, you already saw me leaving together with Jonathan earlier, so why bother asking me now?"
Lucia immediately rolled her eyes after hearing that answer.
Clearly, she was not satisfied with his response at all.
However, before either of them could continue questioning him, Max calmly spoke again.
"Anyway," he said, "please inform Master that I will not be attending tomorrow’s banquet."
Both Isabella and Lucia looked slightly surprised after hearing that.
"I will be busy training," Max added calmly.
After saying that, Max no longer stayed outside.
He directly walked past the two of them and headed toward his room inside the mansion.
Soon, after entering his room, Max immediately noticed a storage ring placed neatly on the table nearby.
A faint smile instantly appeared across his face.
Clearly, these were the rewards distributed after the Smelting Trial ended.
Without wasting time, Max picked up the storage ring and inspected its contents.
The moment his consciousness entered the ring, his eyes brightened immediately.

Inside were enormous amounts of cultivation resources, rare treasures, divine crystals, and numerous valuable materials obtained both from the Smelting Trial rewards and the treasures he personally recorded inside the Tower of Treasure.
Seeing such a massive collection of resources gathered together, even Max could not help revealing a satisfied smile.
"Nice," Max muttered softly.
"With this much treasure, I should finally be able to enter the peak of the Law Awakening Realm."
At the same time, anticipation gradually appeared within his eyes.
"And after that..."
A faint draconic aura unconsciously flickered around his body.
"I can finally open the fourth Divine Vein of the Seven Divine Veins."
"The Vein of Speed."

The moment his consciousness entered the ring, his eyes brightened immediately.

Inside were enormous amounts of cultivation resources, rare treasures, divine crystals, and numerous valuable materials obtained both from the Smelting Trial rewards and the treasures he personally recorded inside the Tower of Treasure.
Seeing such a massive collection of resources gathered together, even Max could not help revealing a satisfied smile.
"Nice," Max muttered softly.
"With this much treasure, I should finally be able to enter the peak of the Law Awakening Realm."
At the same time, anticipation gradually appeared within his eyes.
"And after that..."
A faint draconic aura unconsciously flickered around his body.
"I can finally open the fourth Divine Vein of the Seven Divine Veins."
"The Vein of Speed."

chapters.title: Chapter 1674: Practicing Saint Origin Sword Art
paragraphs: Max did not immediately use the enormous amount of resources he had just obtained to raise his cultivation to the tenth level of the Law Awakening Realm.
Neither did he rush to unlock the fourth Divine Vein, the Vein of Speed.
Although both breakthroughs were extremely tempting, Max still forcibly restrained himself.
Because at this moment, there was something he considered even more important.
The Saint Origin Sword Art.
After entering the Dimension of Time, Max devoted all of his focus entirely toward comprehending and practicing the sword art left behind by the Sword Saint.
The more he practiced it, the more Max realized how terrifying and profound this sword art truly was.
Every movement.
Every slash.
Every fluctuation of sword intent hidden within the technique seemed to contain layers upon layers of deeper mysteries.

At first glance, the Saint Origin Sword Art appeared straightforward and overbearing, yet the more Max tried to master it, the more he felt as though he had merely touched the surface of an endless ocean.
This realization only made Max even more serious.
After all, this was not some ordinary sword technique.
It was the personal sword art created by the Sword Saint himself.
A legendary existence whose name alone was enough to shake countless worlds.
Because of that, Max became completely immersed within the Saint Origin Sword Art.
Inside the endless flow of time within the Dimension of Time, Max continuously practiced the sword art again and again without pause.
At times, he practiced ordinary slashes.
At other times, he attempted to fuse the Emotion Severing Cosmic Path into the sword art once more.
Slowly, Max began noticing things he had previously overlooked.
The Saint Origin Sword Art was not simply about destructive power.
It carried a strange sense of purity and sharpness capable of severing everything in existence.
The deeper Max comprehended it, the more terrifying the sword art gradually became.
Because of this, Max spent the entire night after the Smelting Trial completely immersed within the Dimension of Time practicing continuously.
He ignored rest entirely.
He ignored cultivation advancement.
Even the temptation of unlocking the Vein of Speed was temporarily pushed aside.
Nothing mattered more to him right now than fully understanding the Saint Origin Sword Art.
It was not until the following morning that Max finally left the Dimension of Time.
And even then, it was not because he wanted to stop practicing.
In truth, Max still wished to continue comprehending the sword art further.
However, someone had arrived outside his room earlier and informed him that Jonathan wished to speak with him again.
Because of that, Max had no choice but to temporarily leave the Dimension of Time and leave the mansion as well.
Not long afterward, Max arrived at the same pavilion where Jonathan had brought him the previous day.
The quiet spirit lake still reflected the soft morning light while the surrounding breeze carried a calm and peaceful atmosphere.
However, the moment Max stepped into the pavilion, he immediately noticed something completely different about Jonathan and Julie.
Yesterday, both of them had been surrounded by gloom, tension, and helplessness.
But today—
Those emotions were completely gone.
Bright smiles could clearly be seen on both of their faces while even the atmosphere around them felt noticeably lighter than before.
Especially Julie.

The previous instability hidden within her aura had vanished almost entirely. Instead, faint crimson poison flames occasionally flickered subtly around her body before disappearing once again under her complete control.
Seeing this scene, Max instantly understood the outcome.
They had chosen to trust him.
A faint smile slowly appeared across Max’s face afterward.
"It seems the two of you are in quite a good mood today," Max said calmly as he walked into the pavilion.
The moment Jonathan saw him, the usually composed young man immediately stood up.
Then, to Max’s surprise, Jonathan directly looked at him with an expression filled with genuine gratitude.
"It worked," Jonathan said while smiling brightly. "The Chaos Fruit truly worked!"
Even now, traces of disbelief could still be seen within his eyes as though he still found the entire situation unreal.
Julie also looked toward Max with gratitude visible within her gaze.
Jonathan quickly continued speaking afterward.
"After Julie consumed the Chaos Fruit last night, the poison inside her body immediately began reacting violently with the flame energy contained within the fruit."
"At first, we thought something had gone wrong because the poison fluctuations became extremely unstable."
Jonathan let out a breath before continuing.
"But then her Ten Thousand Poison Body suddenly began mutating."
The excitement within his voice became increasingly obvious.
"The poison physique and the flame energy from the Chaos Fruit fused together completely and eventually created an entirely new Divine Body."
Jonathan’s eyes brightened noticeably afterward.
"The Ten Thousand Poison Flame Body."
The moment those words were spoken, even the surrounding energy inside the pavilion seemed to fluctuate faintly.
Meanwhile, Julie slowly raised her hand.
In the next instant, crimson poisonous flames silently appeared above her palm.
The flames looked extremely dangerous, yet they remained completely stable beneath her control.
Not even the slightest trace of poison leaked outward anymore.
Seeing this, Jonathan’s expression became even more emotional.

"You have no idea how unbelievable this is," he said while looking toward Max. "Before this, Julie constantly needed treasures to suppress the poison inside her body. Even then, controlling the poison was incredibly difficult."
"But now..."
Jonathan looked toward Julie again before smiling.
"She can control the poison as naturally as controlling her own energy."
"The poison no longer harms her body anymore. Instead, it has completely fused with her new Divine Body."
At that moment, even Julie herself looked slightly emotional.
For the first time in many years, she no longer needed to fear the poison inside her own body and just like Max had said yesterday, it had now become her strongest weapon.
"Good." Max was truly happy for them. He then asked about his deal. "What about my two conditions?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1675: Poisoned Ray!
paragraphs: After hearing Max’s words, Jonathan slowly straightened his posture.
The hesitation and uncertainty from yesterday had completely disappeared from his expression. What replaced it now was determination.
"Since Julie has already been cured," Jonathan said seriously while looking directly at Max, "it is only right that we fulfill our side of the agreement as well."
Then he continued without hesitation.
"Max, we are prepared to join your secret force."
A faint smile appeared across Max’s face after hearing that.
At the same time, Jonathan’s expression gradually turned colder.
"As for your first condition..." Jonathan said quietly, "come with us."
His eyes narrowed faintly afterward.
"Everything has already been arranged."
The moment those words fell, both Jonathan and Julie turned around and began walking deeper into the pavilion area.
Max calmly followed behind them while silently observing the increasingly secluded surroundings.
The deeper they went, the quieter the atmosphere became.
Soon, Jonathan led Max toward a hidden passage concealed beneath the pavilion itself.
After entering the underground area, the surroundings immediately became dark and cold.

There were no artificial lights illuminating the underground pathways. Instead, old burning torches lined the stone walls on both sides, causing flickering flames to cast long shadows throughout the tunnels.
The entire place carried an ancient and gloomy atmosphere.
It resembled some sort of forgotten underground ruin hidden beneath the Violet Star Palace.
"What exactly is this place?" Max asked curiously while looking around the dim underground tunnels.
Julie answered calmly while continuing forward.
"This is a hidden location beneath the Violet Star Palace," she explained. "A very long time ago, this area was used as a prison."
Her voice became slightly colder afterward.
"Those who committed crimes severe enough to warrant execution were imprisoned here."
Max’s eyes flickered slightly.
"Later, after countless years passed, the location was abandoned and gradually forgotten by most people inside the Violet Star Palace."
Max slowly nodded after hearing that explanation.
The deeper they traveled into the underground tunnels, the more the place genuinely resembled an old prison.
Cold stone walls.
Narrow passageways.
Heavy metal doors.
The atmosphere itself carried traces of despair and suffering left behind from the past.
Eventually, after passing through several underground corridors, the three of them arrived before a dark cave-like chamber.
The moment Max stepped closer, he immediately sensed violent fluctuations coming from inside.
Boom!
Boom!
Boom!
Inside the cave, a young man was frantically punching the stone walls repeatedly.
The entire chamber shook faintly under the force of his attacks.
Then suddenly, after hearing footsteps approaching, the young man abruptly turned around.
The moment his eyes landed on Jonathan, Julie, and Max, his expression twisted violently.
"Jonathan! Julie!" Ray roared furiously.
However, unlike his arrogant appearance during the Smelting Trial, Ray now looked completely miserable.
His voice sounded hoarse and weak.
His hair was disheveled.
The color within his eyes had dimmed noticeably.
Even his skin had turned faintly purple.
At a single glance, anyone could tell something was terribly wrong with his condition.
"I feel weak throughout my entire body!" Ray shouted while staggering slightly. "Even the world around me keeps spinning!"
His furious gaze locked directly onto Jonathan.
"What exactly did you put inside the drink you gave me?!"
The moment those words fell, Max immediately understood the situation.
Ray had been poisoned.
"Did the two of you poison him using one of your poisons, Julie?" Max asked while calmly observing Ray’s miserable condition.
At that moment, Ray no longer resembled the arrogant genius from the Smelting Trial at all.
His entire body looked weak and unstable while traces of purple poison continuously spread beneath his skin. Even the spiritual energy fluctuations around him had become chaotic and disordered.
Jonathan nodded slowly after hearing Max’s question.
"Yes," he admitted without hiding anything.
Then he let out a helpless breath before continuing.
"We originally did not know how to deal with him."
Jonathan’s expression gradually became more serious afterward.
"Ray is slightly stronger than either of us individually. Though we can handle him if two of us can take actions together but that would create too much chaos."
Julie also spoke quietly at that moment.
"And if he escaped," she said calmly, "everything would become troublesome afterward."
After all, Ray was not an ordinary genius.

Not only was he powerful himself, but he also possessed the backing of the Sword God Palace. Once someone like him became alert and cautious, dealing with him secretly would become extremely difficult.
Because of that, Jonathan and Julie could not afford to fail.
Jonathan continued speaking afterward.
"So in the end, we decided to take a risk."
His gaze slowly shifted toward Julie.
"After Julie awakened the Ten Thousand Poison Flame Body last night, her control over poison improved tremendously."
Jonathan’s expression still carried traces of disbelief while speaking about it.

"The difference was unbelievable. Before this, even Julie herself struggled to completely control the poison within her body. But after awakening the new Divine Body, she became capable of manipulating poison with astonishing precision."
Julie calmly nodded afterward.
"Because of that," she explained softly, "we decided to test one of my new poisons on Ray."
A faint coldness flashed within her eyes.
"We invited him earlier under the excuse of discussing matters related to the Smelting Trial and the coming banquet."
Jonathan smiled faintly afterward.
"Fortunately, he never suspected us."
"Ray drank the poisoned wine without noticing anything unusual."
Jonathan then looked toward Ray once again.
"And apparently..."
A faint smile slowly appeared on his face.
"It worked far better than we expected."
A faint smile slowly appeared across Max’s face after hearing Jonathan and Julie’s explanation.
"You two handled this quite well," Max said calmly while looking toward the miserable Ray standing inside the chamber.
Then Max’s gaze slowly shifted back toward Jonathan and Julie.
"Now," he continued with a faintly amused smile, "would the two of you mind leaving us alone for a while?"
His eyes briefly moved toward Ray afterward.
"I would like to spend some personal time with him."
Jonathan and Julie immediately understood what Max meant.
Neither of them said anything further.
Instead, they simply exchanged a brief glance before shrugging lightly and turning around to leave the underground chamber together.
However, the moment Ray realized they were truly walking away, panic and fury instantly exploded across his face.
"Jonathan! Julie!" Ray roared loudly.
His voice echoed throughout the underground chamber while his already disheveled appearance became even more frantic.
At that moment, Ray finally understood what was happening.
He had been completely betrayed.
The people he trusted enough to drink with had secretly poisoned him and handed him directly over to Max.
The realization caused his eyes to turn bloodshot instantly.
"I trusted the two of you!" Ray shouted furiously while staggering forward weakly. "And this is how you repay me?!"
The hatred and disbelief within his voice became increasingly intense.
"You actually sold me out to Max!"
Ray’s face twisted violently with rage afterward.
"How dare you do this to me?!"
Then, as though suddenly remembering his own background, Ray immediately began roaring threateningly.
"Once the Sword God Palace learns about this, both of you are dead!"
Terrifying hatred filled his eyes completely.
"The Sword God Palace will never forgive this betrayal!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1676: Taking Care of Ray!
paragraphs: After Jonathan and Julie completely left the underground chamber, silence gradually returned once again.
Only Max and Ray remained inside the dark prison-like cave now.
The flickering torch flames hanging along the stone walls cast long moving shadows throughout the chamber while Ray continued breathing heavily from the poison spreading inside his body.
His condition had clearly worsened compared to earlier. Purple poison veins spread visibly beneath his skin while his spiritual aura fluctuated chaotically without stability.
Meanwhile, Max calmly walked forward step by step until he finally stopped directly in front of Ray.
Then he spoke quietly.
"Before you die, there is something I want to know."
Ray slowly raised his head after hearing those words.
Hatred and killing intent immediately filled his bloodshot eyes the moment he looked at Max.
"Who exactly from the Sword God Palace ordered you to kill me?" Max asked calmly.
The moment those words entered Ray’s ears, his expression changed slightly.
Although the change was brief, Max still noticed it clearly.
However, that hesitation quickly disappeared and was replaced by a cold sneer afterward.
"You think I would tell you something like that?" Ray laughed hoarsely while glaring at Max hatefully.
Even in his miserable state, arrogance still remained deeply rooted within him.
"You really have no idea what kind of existence the Sword God Palace truly is," Ray continued coldly.
His face gradually twisted more and more while hatred filled his voice.
"If I die here, the Sword God Palace will never let you go."
"The people standing behind me are existences far beyond your imagination."
Ray continued threatening Max repeatedly while relying entirely upon the reputation and power of the Sword God Palace.
"The moment they discover what happened to me, your fate will become worse than death."
"You actually think someone like you can oppose the Sword God Palace?"
Ray suddenly burst into crazed laughter.
"You are nothing in front of them!"
However, throughout the entire exchange, Max’s expression remained completely calm.
He simply observed Ray quietly while pondering silently in his mind.
Since Ray refused to reveal the truth willingly, Max could only speculate himself.
Deep down, Max already possessed a strong suspicion regarding the identity of the person behind all this.
Mira.
The daughter of the Sword God Palace.
From the beginning, she had shown obvious hostility toward him, especially after the matter involving the Dragonheart Sword and what had happened between them in Orion.
Everything pointed toward her.
However—
Another possibility suddenly surfaced within Max’s mind.
Could there perhaps be someone else involved as well?
Someone else within the Sword God Palace who also wanted him dead?
That thought caused Max’s eyes to narrow slightly.
Then slowly, a faint smile appeared across his face.
"If you refuse to answer," Max said calmly, "then I will simply find the answer myself."
Before Ray could properly understand what Max meant, Max suddenly raised his right hand and directly placed it upon Ray’s head.
The moment Max touched him, Ray’s expression changed drastically.
An overwhelming sense of danger exploded within his heart instantly.
"What are you doing?!" Ray shouted instinctively.
However, before he could react further—
Boom!!!
A terrifying wave of soul force erupted violently from Max’s body.
The entire underground chamber trembled faintly while strange soul fluctuations spread throughout the surroundings. Even the torch flames along the walls flickered chaotically beneath the pressure.
Then suddenly—
Ray screamed.
"AAAAAAHHHHHH!!!"
An incomparably painful scream echoed throughout the underground prison as a translucent figure was forcefully dragged out from within Ray’s body.
It was his soul.
Ray’s soul struggled frantically while emitting terrified screams, but it was completely unable to resist the overwhelming authority of the Dimension of Soul.
At that moment, Max’s eyes glowed faintly while terrifying soul laws silently activated around him.
The next instant, Ray’s soul was directly pulled into the Dimension of Soul.
Inside that mysterious dimension, everything immediately changed.

The moment Ray’s soul entered the Dimension of Soul, it became completely suppressed by the laws governing that place. Invisible soul chains instantly wrapped around it while terrifying refining power descended from every direction.
Ray’s soul struggled desperately.
He screamed.
He begged.
However, nothing could stop the refining process.
Soon afterward, the Dimension of Soul began breaking Ray’s soul apart gradually and refining it into pure soul force.
At the same time, Max immediately felt enormous amounts of refined soul energy flowing directly into his sea of consciousness.
His soul force began increasing rapidly.
The strength of his soul became noticeably more powerful while pure soul energy continuously nourished every corner of his consciousness.
However, that was not the only thing Max obtained.
As Ray’s soul continued being refined completely, countless memories suddenly flooded directly into Max’s mind.
Scenes began flashing rapidly one after another.
Conversations.
Orders.
Hatred.
Plans.
Killing intent.
Max silently watched through all of Ray’s memories while searching for the answer he wanted.
Then eventually—
He saw her.
Mira.
The daughter of the Sword God Palace.
Inside Ray’s memories, Max clearly witnessed Mira personally instructing Ray to kill him during the Smelting Trial. The hatred within her eyes while speaking about Max was unmistakable.
The moment Max saw those memories, a cold smile slowly appeared across his face.
"So it truly was you," Max muttered quietly.
Knowing that the person behind everything was indeed Mira, Max did not feel particularly surprised.
From the very beginning, he had already suspected her involvement. After witnessing the memories extracted from Ray’s soul, that suspicion had merely been confirmed completely.
Because of that, Max no longer wasted any further thought on the matter.
Instead, his gaze slowly shifted toward Ray’s lifeless body lying on the cold stone floor.
Then—
Black flames suddenly erupted from Max’s hand.

The dark flames radiated terrifying devouring energy as they instantly engulfed Ray’s corpse completely. The moment the flames touched the body, Ray’s flesh, blood, bones, and even remaining spiritual energy began rapidly disintegrating.
Within only a few moments, Ray’s body was completely devoured into nothingness.
At the same time, a dense stream of energy immediately surged back into Max’s body through the black flames.
